title: Titanic wireless and ships 1912 source-first shot-by-shot visual edit
reference_narration: Existing 10 unmodified Kokoro paragraphs T08_P01 to T08_P10

shots.onscreen_label: HAROLD BRIDE · TITANIC'S JUNIOR WIRELESS OPERATOR
shots.editorial_why: Genuine portrait of Titanic radio operator whose equipment connected ship to shore; portrait date is circa 1911–1913, not a photograph at the transmitter.

shots.onscreen_label: TWO WIRELESS OPERATORS · PHOTOGRAPHED AFTER RESCUE
shots.editorial_why: Harold Bride and Carpathia wireless operator Harold Cottam actually pictured together after the disaster; people named, not a made-up 1912 wireless room.

shots.onscreen_label: 15 APRIL 1912 · TITANIC DISTRESS SIGNAL RECORD
shots.editorial_why: Actual UK National Archives wireless signal associated with Jack Phillips; historical document directly supports CQD/SOS discussion without falsely implying first-ever use.

shots.onscreen_label: CAPTAIN ROSTRON'S HANDWRITTEN ACCOUNT · 27 APRIL 1912
shots.editorial_why: Genuine account describing Carpathia's response; document dates are after sinking and don't pretend this is a raw contemporaneous ship signal.

shots.onscreen_label: CARPATHIA'S 15 APRIL NAUTICAL CHART · HISTORIC RECORD
shots.editorial_why: Actual navigation source associated with Carpathia, relevant to positions and clock conversions; modern captions separately labelled.

shots.onscreen_label: SHIP TIMES ≠ SHORE TIMES · SOURCE ATTRIBUTED
shots.editorial_why: Authentic photos do not explain different nautical and shore clocks; a labelled uncertainty/timing diagram is required.

shots.onscreen_label: ARTHUR HENRY ROSTRON · CAPTAIN OF CARPATHIA
shots.editorial_why: Actual portrait of the rescue captain while in Carpathia service; does not depict his orders at sea.

shots.onscreen_label: CARPATHIA'S CAPTAIN AND OFFICERS · AFTER THE RESCUE
shots.editorial_why: Actual dated group of rescue ship officers, not a manufactured view of their preparations during the disaster.

shots.onscreen_label: SS CALIFORNIAN · PERIOD PHOTOGRAPH FROM NARA
shots.editorial_why: Actual Calder Californian photograph; source cautiously says may have been taken from Carpathia after joining rescue; not proof of precise distance during sinking.

shots.onscreen_label: CAPTAIN STANLEY LORD · AT THE BRITISH INQUIRY
shots.editorial_why: Authentic May 1912 British enquiry press record of Californian captain; matches disputed radio watch and rocket testimony.

shots.onscreen_label: THE BRITISH WRECK COMMISSIONER'S INQUIRY · 1912
shots.editorial_why: Real inquiry hall illustrates precisely the institution drawing the criticized Californian conclusions, not a courtroom recreation.

shots.onscreen_label: BRITISH REPORT VS LATER INTERPRETATION
shots.editorial_why: A source-labelled comparison is required since real inquiry room photos do not establish positions or settle historians' later debate.

shots.onscreen_label: CAPTAIN LORD QUESTIONED · BRITISH INQUIRY (REVISITED)
shots.editorial_why: Deliberate closer crop of exact original testimony-related portrait as the narrator distinguishes finding from certainty; photographic reuse is explicitly flagged.

shots.onscreen_label: THE EXACT DISTANCE WAS DISPUTED
shots.editorial_why: The inquiry and later analyses disagree; geographic uncertainty cannot honestly be photographed in 1912, only schematically explained.

shots.onscreen_label: WIRELESS OPERATOR BRIDE AFTER THE SINKING · 1912
shots.editorial_why: Genuine injured survivor photograph illustrates the later documented human cost of operators' service; explicitly labelled AFTER, not an image of him operating at the time.

shots.onscreen_label: WIRELESS COULD CALL FOR HELP · NOT EMPTY THE SHIP
shots.editorial_why: A source-anchored roles/limits graphic directly contrasts what distress calls could and could not accomplish.

shots.onscreen_label: A SURVIVING SIGNAL RECORD · SOURCE REVISITED
shots.editorial_why: Different close focus on the actual UK National Archives signal emphasises provenance and transcription uncertainty, not a second fictitious record.

shots.onscreen_label: STATION LOGS REQUIRE CROSS-CHECKING
shots.editorial_why: Source-chain infographic needed because a single document does not establish every received message, minute or copying error.

shots.onscreen_label: CARPATHIA AT NEW YORK · AFTER TITANIC RESCUE
shots.editorial_why: The actual vessel that answered the distress, photographed following rescue. Caption carefully distinguishes post-rescue view from the midnight response.

shots.onscreen_label: DISTRESS REACHED SHIPS · RESCUE STILL TOO LATE
shots.editorial_why: Original source-timed interval diagram required; no authentic photo of that voyage can establish when the ship arrived relative to sinking.

editorial_type: Fixed bespoke editor selections; NO automated keyword matching or montages
cautions: Captain Rostron's written account is dated after the sinking, not a live wireless log
UK Archive Titanic signal original document should not be labelled first-ever SOS
Californian historical photograph does not resolve its distance
Harold Bride wounded photo was AFTER the disaster
Captain Lord photograph repeated only for explicitly distinct enquiry finding and later uncertainty beats
